methods.label: Bound a positive ratio
methods.explanation:
Changing to a positive denominator makes the bounds easier to use. Let \(t=-x\), so \(2\le t\le4\). In particular, neither \(x\) nor \(t\) is zero, and
\[\frac{x+y}{x}=1-\frac{y}{t}.\]
To maximize this expression, we want to make the positive ratio \(y/t\) as small as possible. Since \(y\ge2\) and \(0<t\le4\),
\[\frac{y}{t}\ge\frac{2}{t}\ge\frac{2}{4}=\frac12.\]
Therefore \(1-y/t\le1/2\). Equality holds when \(y=2\) and \(t=4\), corresponding to the allowed values \(x=-4\) and \(y=2\). The largest possible value is \(\boxed{\frac12}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
